qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Quotations (RFQ) issued by the NYS Office of General Services for an Aggregate Hardware Buy, including competitive quotes, submission deadlines, evaluation criteria, and terms and conditions.

quotes.quote: RFQ Title Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 RFQ Number 20-01
Request for Quotations 20-01

OGS is seeking competitive quotes from Contract holders of the OGS Group 73600 Award 22802 Information Technology Umbrella Contract – Manufacturer Based (Statewide) (“Manufacturer Umbrella Contract”) for the Lots indicated below.
The purpose of RFQ 20-01 is to establish an award for each Configuration as set forth in Attachment A - Technical Response.
Quotes and pricing submitted in response to  RFQ 20-01 must remain open and valid for at least one hundred-twenty (120) calendar days from the date that RFQ Submissions are due

findings.title: Discount Percentage Applicability to Additional Products
findings.fact: Section 7.2.5 states that the same awarded discount percentages that applied to the three Required Product categories shall apply to Additional Products in their respective categories. However, Section 6.2.1 states that pricing for Additional Products will not be factored into the evaluation, but submission of items for review at the time of bid will facilitate the availability of Additional Products for Authorized Users as part of a Configuration at time of award.
findings.business_implication: There may be ambiguity regarding whether Additional Products are subject to the same discount percentages as Required Products, which could affect pricing strategy.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from OGS on how discount percentages apply to Additional Products and whether they are mandatory.

quotes.quote: Contractors shall provide the same awarded discount percentages that applied to the three (3) Required Product categories (Warranty and Services, Components, and Peripherals), to the Additional Products in their respective categories.

Pricing for any Additional Products will not be factored into the evaluation, but submission of items for review at the time of bid will facilitate the availability of Additional Products for Authorized Users as part of a Configuration at time of award.

findings.title: Number of Standard Configurations Discrepancy
findings.fact: Page 6 lists five Standard Configurations (1-5), while page 9 states 'Contractors may bid on one, some, or all fourteen (14) Standard Configurations.'
findings.business_implication: The bidder needs to know the actual number of configurations to prepare the technical response.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with OGS the correct number of Standard Configurations.

findings.title: Delivery Extension Approval Process
findings.fact: The RFQ states that the Authorized User may grant an extension up to 60 days, but also states that extensions beyond 60 days require OGS approval. There is potential ambiguity regarding who has authority for extensions between 45 and 60 days.
findings.business_implication: The bidder may face uncertainty in obtaining delivery extensions, impacting planning.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify the extension approval process with OGS during the clarification period.

quotes.quote: If upon receipt of a Purchase Order the Awarded Contractor determines it cannot meet the 45 calendar day delivery period the Awarded Contractor may submit a written request to the Authorized User to extend the required Product delivery period to up to sixty (60) calendar days. The Authorized User shall respond in writing to the Awarded Contractor either declining the request or specifying the revised delivery period.

If an Authorized User wants to extend the delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days, the Authorized User may submit a written request to extend the Product delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days to OGS for its approval.

findings.title: Delivery Extension Approval Process
findings.fact: The document states that if an Authorized User wants to extend the delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days, the Authorized User may submit a written request to extend the Product delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days to OGS for its approval. However, it also states that approval of substantially delayed deliveries (over 60 calendar days) will be limited to delays that are a result of an industry wide event or other acceptable extenuating circumstance, that limits or prohibits Contractor’s ability to deliver within Agreement delivery timeframes. This could be interpreted as requiring OGS approval for any extension beyond 60 days, but the criteria for approval are restrictive.
findings.business_implication: The bidder may face uncertainty regarding the ability to obtain extensions for delays beyond 60 days, as approval is at OGS's sole discretion and limited to specific circumstances.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with OGS the process and criteria for obtaining extensions beyond 60 days to ensure understanding and compliance.

quotes.quote: If an Authorized User wants to extend the delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days, the Authorized User may submit a written request to extend the Product delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days to OGS for its approval.

Approval of substantially delayed deliveries (over 60 calendar days), when the delayed delivery will impact more than one order fulfillment in a thirty (30) day time frame for more than 75 calendar days per incident, will be limited to delays that are a result of an industry wide event or other acceptable extenuating circumstance, that limits or prohibits Contractor’s ability to deliver within Agreement delivery timeframes.
